# example:weather-client

<!-- Generated by crucible. Change the model or the SDK configuration and regenerate. -->

The Kotlin client for the Weather API (`example.weather#Weather`, API version `2026-10-01`, sent as `Crucible-Version: 2026-10-01` on every request), generated by [Crucible](https://github.com/Operation-Leyline/crucible) from the service's model.

## Install

```kotlin
implementation("example:weather-client:0.0.0-dev")
```

The package is `example:weather-client`, version `0.0.0-dev`; code refers to it as `example.weather`.

## Create a client

```kotlin
import example.weather.WeatherClient
import example.weather.ClientConfig
import example.weather.model.*

val client = WeatherClient(ClientConfig(token = { System.getenv("WEATHER_TOKEN") }))
```

`ClientConfig.token` is a `suspend` function returning the bearer token, called for every attempt, so a refreshed token is used. The client is `AutoCloseable`; share one instance. The client sends `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and `Crucible-Version: 2026-10-01` on every request.

## Call an operation

`getCity` calls `GetCity`. Every operation has a method like it.

```kotlin
import example.weather.ClientConfig
import example.weather.WeatherClient
import example.weather.model.*
import kotlin.time.ExperimentalTime
import kotlin.time.Instant

@OptIn(ExperimentalTime::class)
suspend fun main() {
    // The client sends Authorization: Bearer <token> and Crucible-Version: 2026-10-01 on every request.
    val client = WeatherClient(ClientConfig(token = { System.getenv("WEATHER_TOKEN") }))

    // Values from the model's example "Read a city".
    val input = GetCityInput {
        cityId = "c-0a1b2c3d"
        at = Instant.parse("2026-01-02T03:04:05Z")
    }

    try {
        val output = client.getCity(input)
        println(output.city)
        println(output.forecast)
        println(output.requestIdValue)
    } catch (error: NotFoundError) {
        System.err.println("NotFoundError (HTTP ${error.status}): ${error.messageValue}")
    }
}
```

## Pagination

A paginated operation also has a `<operation>Pages` method returning a cold `Flow` of pages (`client.listCitiesPages(input).collect { page -> ... }`): each page is one response, and it stops when the response carries no next token. Every operation is a `suspend` function, called from a coroutine; each also takes the input's DSL block (`client.getCity { ... }`).

```kotlin
import example.weather.ClientConfig
import example.weather.WeatherClient
import example.weather.model.*

suspend fun main() {
    // The client sends Authorization: Bearer <token> and Crucible-Version: 2026-10-01 on every request.
    val client = WeatherClient(ClientConfig(token = { System.getenv("WEATHER_TOKEN") }))

    // Values from the model's example "List the first page".
    val input = ListCitiesInput {
        maxResults = 2
        tags = listOf("coastal", "capital")
    }

    // Each page is one response; the flow sends `nextToken` for the next.
    client.listCitiesPages(input).collect { page ->
        println(page.cities)
    }
}
```

## Errors

Each modelled error is an exception class in `example.weather.model`, extending `example.weather.WeatherException` and `ServiceError`: catch it and read its properties, and `status`, `requestId` and `headers`. A modelled member named like an exception property takes a `Value` suffix (`messageValue`). Transport failures throw `NetworkError`.

## Retries and idempotency

Calls are retried with backoff when a retry is safe: a modelled throttling error is retried for any operation; transport failures, HTTP 500, 502, 503 and 504 and other retryable modelled errors only for operations that are read-only, idempotent or carry an idempotency token. For operations that declare an idempotency token, an unset token is generated once per call and reused on every attempt; set it yourself to replay one logical request across calls. These operations fill a token: `createCity` (`clientToken`). Set `maxAttempts` in `ClientConfig` to change the attempt limit (3, the first included; 1 turns retries off), `timeout`, `baseDelay` and `maxDelay` for the call budget and backoff, and `retryMode` to `RetryMode.STANDARD` or `RetryMode.ADAPTIVE` for a shared retry quota or client-side rate limiting.
